stem: In a circle with center $M$, $\overline{AB}$ and $\overline{AC}$ are two chords. $MD\perp\overline{AB}$ at $D$ and $ME\perp\overline{AC}$ at $E$, and $MD=ME$. If $AD=(2x+{=p})$ cm and $AE=(3x-{=q})$ cm, find the length of $\overline{AB}$ in cm.
solution: MD = ME, so the chords AB and AC are equidistant from the center, so AB = AC (converse).
D and E are the midpoints of AB and AC (a perpendicular from the center bisects the chord), so AD = AE.
notes: Advanced: converse, then half-chords equal, solve linear equation, double. q=x-p guarantees AD=AE=e at the chosen x; AE = 3x-q = 2x+p.
